label: D1 after a reward, when the agent is about to choose a1, late in the episode
explanation: Fires only at D1, never at GO or D2. 82% of activation mass falls on D1 steps where the reward input is 1. It is strongly biased toward a1: 93% of mass is on trials where the agent goes on to choose a1, and the good state is S1 for 82% of mass. It is also restricted to late episodes: there are no activations before about trial 20, and the rate climbs to a peak around trials 80-89. In the example windows the activation ramps up over a run of rewarded a1 trials and often persists, somewhat weaker, into the D1 right after an unrewarded trial, so it looks like a slowly building trace of being rewarded for a1. The predicate uses action at D1, which is the agent own upcoming choice; that is allowed, and it was preferred because it scored better (dev F1 0.62, mass recall 0.80) than the purely observed prev_action == 1 variant (F1 0.54, mass recall 0.61), which loses the first trial of each window. No future random outcome is used. Allowing in_rew == 0 when the reward two trials back was 1 raises mass recall to 0.88 but lowers precision to 0.49. False positives are mainly early rewarded a1 trials, before the trace has built up; many episodes fire weakly or not at all. Magnitude is lower when the model value output is high (no activations above value 7.73).

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=D1 & before=a2 S1 r (+2.99), phase=D1 & this=a1 S1 (+2.93), phase=D1 & this=a1 S2 (+2.85), phase=D1 & ep_dec=8 (+2.71), phase=D1 & rel=1 (+2.15), phase=D1 & choice_bin=decile 5 (9 = most a1) (+2.10). Lower it: prev_state=2 (-10.52), phase=D2 (-5.55), phase=GO (-5.42), before=a2 S2 u (-4.59).
